findings.title: Cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without explanation
findings.body: The ticker interval for the entire cleanup service was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This affects all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history), not just annotations. The PR description does not mention this change, suggesting it may be a debugging leftover. Running all cleanup jobs 10x more frequently will significantly increase database load in production, especially now that annotation cleanup performs multiple round-trip queries per batch.

findings.title: Normal operational logging uses Error level
findings.body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 all use `r.log.Error(...)` to log routine cleanup progress (e.g., "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time"). These are not errors — they represent normal operation. In production, this will flood error-level logs and trigger false alerts in monitoring systems that alert on error log volume. These should be `Debug` or `Info` level.

findings.title: SQLite parameter limit check uses batch size instead of actual ID count
findings.body: The condition `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` checks the configured batch size rather than `len(ids)`. If the batch size is configured above 999 but fewer IDs are actually returned (e.g., only 50 rows match), the code unnecessarily inlines IDs into the SQL string instead of using parameterized queries. The check should be `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit` to correctly decide based on the actual number of parameters that will be bound.

findings.title: Race between fetchIDs and deleteByIDs may cause premature loop termination
findings.body: Because fetchIDs and deleteByIDs run in separate sessions (no shared transaction), another process could delete the fetched IDs between the SELECT and DELETE. If this happens for an entire batch, `deleteByIDs` returns 0 affected rows, and `untilDoneOrCancelled` terminates the loop — even if more annotations still qualify for cleanup. The code comment acknowledges under-deletion from concurrent inserts, but this scenario (concurrent deletes causing early termination) means the cleanup may stop prematurely and not resume until the next scheduled cycle. With the ticker now at 1 minute this is less impactful, but worth documenting.

findings.title: Test uses explicit IDs that may conflict across test runs on shared databases
findings.body: The `createTestAnnotations` function now sets `ID: int64(i + 1)` explicitly. If tests run against a shared database where the auto-increment sequence has advanced past these IDs (e.g., from a previous partial run or parallel test), the explicit IDs could conflict. The cleanup between subtests deletes all rows, but if a test panics before cleanup runs, subsequent runs may fail with duplicate key errors. Using the database's auto-increment (as the old code did) would be more robust.
